item.title: 5 Near-Perfect PS2 FPS Games No One Played
item.description:
The PlayStation 2 's legacy doesn't heavily feature first-person shooters, but the console wasn't a bad home for the genre. TimeSplitters 2, Nightfire , Black , and Killzone were fairly big, even if they haven't all stood the test of time. Still, great PS2 FPS games were in relatively short supply, and there's very little reason to revisit them in this day and age.

Considering the lack of heavy competition, you might think that every fantastic PS2 FPS game had to be a guaranteed hit, but that was far from the case. Plenty of shooters flopped commercially, a side effect of releasing during the genre's highly competitive golden era and on a system better known for JRPGs. Well, let's shine a spotlight on those titles that failed to hit the mainstream mark 20 years ago.

Obviously, "no one played" is hyperbolic, as many folks loved and still love these games. However, they were all financial disappointments and didn't really find a significant audience.

Urban Chaos: Riot Response Is Rocksteady's Solitary FPS Game

A Late-Arrival PS2 Gem That Delivers Aggressive Gameplay

Did you know that Rocksteady existed before Batman ? Yeah, I find that hard to believe as well, but the developer actually had a life before the caped crusader. To be fair, Rocksteady only produced one game before Arkham Asylum , and it didn't have much of an impact on the gaming scene. That said, Urban Chaos: Riot Response is pretty darn awesome and might have done better if it didn't come out in 2006.

24 PS2 Games That Support More Than Two Players

If someone wants to play some classic PlayStation 2 games with friends, these games support more than just 2 players.

1
By Daniel Kurland

In the mid-2000s, the genre consisted almost entirely of military shooters or run-and-gun Doom clones; consequently, Riot Response 's decision to focus on close-quarters arcade combat set it apart from the crowd . Armed with a riot shield that acts as an ever-present wall, you are constantly in a state of both offense and defense, both of which reward aggressive action. While the riot shield blocks almost everything, you need to lower it to shoot, creating a risk-and-reward system.

Riot Response brought quite a few other things to the table. The satirical presentation gives off Judge Dredd or RoboCop vibes, both of which produced far worse PS2 FPS games. The medal-based progression works well, and rescue missions introduce AI first-responders who are actually useful. The gunplay just feels good , too, a statement that can only be made for a handful of console FPS games from this era.

One criticism is that the campaign lasts only about 5 hours, but I honestly don't think that's a negative nowadays. A non-stop brilliant 5 hours is better than a decent 10 hours, and I personally enjoy the occasional game that I can complete in a single day.

Mace Griffin: Bounty Hunter Is Still A Technical Marvel

Shoot Enemies In The Face And Then Dogfight Spaceships

I'll always have time for something called Mace Griffin: Bounty Hunter , as there's nothing I love more than B-movie vibes in an AA game. Now, I'll admit that describing Warthog's 2003 shooter as "near-perfect" is a bit of a stretch, but the game deserves a shout-out for its technical ambition. Don't let the title trick you; Mace Griffin aimed for the stars.

Hybrid games were nothing new by the early 2000s, but none of them had the arrogance to blend spaceship dogfights with on-foot FPS sections quite like this. Mace Griffin lets you swap between the two on the fly , with no load times in between. Most missions are designed to accommodate a variety of approaches, letting players decide how they will complete their objectives.

The actual gunplay doesn't rank among the genre's best as it can be a bit floaty , but it isn't terrible by any stretch of the imagination. It is serviceable without achieving greatness, which is fine since the game's selling point is the genre fusion.

Darkwatch Is Cooler Than Your Favorite FPS Game

Vampires, Gothic Vibes, Anti-Heroes, And High Moon

Darkwatch is the coolest PS2 FPS game, and "PS2" might be an unnecessary qualifier. We are talking about a supernatural western that casts you as Jericho Cross, a recently turned vampire armed with incredible weapons. That entire sentence reeks of awesomeness.

In an era filled with c-grade shooters trying to copy Medal of Honor or Rainbow Six , Darkwatch stood out for its gothic atmosphere , Unreal Tournament -esque gameplay, and willingness to embrace grim silliness. Even in 2026, shooters like Darkwatch are extremely rare, which helps its novelty hold up well. High Moon Studios' pedigree is evident throughout the campaign, with top-notch action, fun character designs, a morality system, and a slightly tongue-in-cheek tone.

Although the PS2 version is worse than the Xbox release, Darkwatch came with split-screen co-op for the full campaign , which is always appreciated.

7 Single-Player FPS Games Completely Erased From History

Some shooters create everlasting legacies, while other FPS games are wiped from existence, barely registering as a footnote in history.

By Mark Sammut

Project: Snowblind Is Simple Sci-Fi Shooter Goodness

A PS2 FPS Game That You Can Easily Play Today

Unlike every other PS2 FPS game in this article, Project: Snowblind can be readily picked up on Steam today, making it the most accessible. Obviously, there are ways to get any PS2 game running on modern systems, but it's nice to have the option to actually buy one.

Born from the ashes of a failed Deus Ex title, Project: Snowblind transplants elements from that franchise into a traditional linear shooter, creating a straightforward FPS romp mostly devoid of the immersive-sim ingredients of its spiritual predecessor. While certainly lacking Deus Ex 's "it" factor, Snowblind gets by on solid gunplay, empowering augmentations, and a toolkit that allows for player expression . Drenched in sci-fi goodness with an urban twist, the weapon arsenal ranks among the better ones of this era, with all the guns being viable.

Although I think the campaign loses a bit of steam towards the end, Project: Snowblind mostly shines as an action-heavy blockbuster that gives players just enough room to experiment.

Cold Winter Is The Best Spy FPS Game On The PS2

007, Eat Your Heart Out (Just Kidding, I Love Nightfire)

Swordfist Studios didn't last long, but it blessed the world with 50 Cent: Blood on the Sand and Cold Winter . The former has a cult following, but the latter tends to be overlooked, despite being comfortably one of the better console-exclusive FPS games of all time. Unlike Bond's glossy adventures, Cold Winter is a visceral espionage shooter fueled by blood and cynicism . It's great.

After being freed from a Chinese gulag, an ex-MI6 operator named Andrew Sterling gets dragged into a global scheme that involves all the spy clichés that you could ever want, albeit presented with unflinching violence. Sterling accomplishes absurd feats, but he doesn't come across as a superhero smashing through armies of men. He is tired and traumatized.

Cold Winter had an impressive-for-its-era cover system, destructible environments, and on-the-fly crafting, all of which were hardly commonplace at the time. The campaign isn't perfectly balanced, and the gunplay feels stiff at times, but these are relatively minor criticisms in the grand scheme of things.

item.title: Gamers Can Win Up to $13,900 By Helping Out Popular Open-World RPG
item.description:
Fans in the Mount & Blade 2 : Bannerlord modding community can win up to €12,000, or roughly $13,900, by creating new content for the RPG as part of TaleWorlds' newly launched War Sails modding competition. TaleWorlds' Mount & Blade 2: Bannerlord combines a large medieval sandbox with trading, diplomacy, kingdom management, and massive real-time battles in which players can fight alongside the armies they command.

Mount & Blade 2 has developed an extensive modding community over the years, with TaleWorlds providing official tools for players who want to create their own additions to Calradia. Those tools recently expanded considerably for owners of War Sails , the game's latest DLC. The expansion introduced naval travel and combat to Bannerlord , allowing players to command ships, fight fleet battles, and wage war across the seas. TaleWorlds subsequently released the War Sails Modding Kit, giving creators access to systems for building naval world maps and developing content around the expansion's new mechanics. The studio is now providing an additional incentive for players to experiment with those tools through its biggest modding competition yet.

Mount & Blade 2 Bannerlord: The Best Companions

Finding the right companion is incredibly important to not only take on the burden in the game but to have someone there to save the player.

By Sid Natividad

Mount & Blade 2 Is Giving Modders a Chance to Win Thousands

The official Mount & Blade 2: War Sails Modding Competition runs from August 14 through November 22, with the largest reward reserved for its Conversion Mod Contest. Both total and partial conversion mods are eligible, meaning entrants can create something like an entirely different setting or substantially transform Bannerlord as part of their entry. Projects are specifically encouraged to use War Sails ' naval travel and battles while introducing new maritime gameplay ideas. The first-place creator can take home €12,000 (roughly $13,900), while TaleWorlds is offering additional prizes of €6,000 ($6,940) and €3,000 ($3,470) for runners-up and a separate €1,000 ($1,160) Community Vote winner.

Perhaps most importantly, entrants don't necessarily need to have a completed mod ready to play. TaleWorlds permits both released and unreleased projects, and an unfinished submission can still be judged on its concept, development plan, and presentation. Participants in the Conversion Mod Contest must upload a public YouTube showcase explaining their project, implemented features, current progress, and plans. Modders can submit as many as three entries, although only their highest-rated project will be considered for the final rankings. TaleWorlds permits teams as well, potentially opening the competition to some of the more ambitious Mount & Blade: 2 Bannerlord conversion mods currently in development.

Modders who aren't interested in building a massive conversion mod still have other ways to compete, albeit with less prize money. Separate 3D Art and Scene Design contests each award €2,000 (about $2,310) for first place, €1,000 ($1,160) for second, and €500 ($580) for third, plus another €500 Community Vote prize. The former challenges creators to design original ships, while the latter focuses on coastal villages built around seaborne raids. That gives artists and level designers opportunities to contribute to Mount & Blade 2 's naval combat without developing an entire campaign overhaul, offering a well-rounded look at the community's different strengths.

First Look at 2 New WWE 2K26 WrestleMania 42 DLC Wrestlers
Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave is Officially Leaving Millions of Players Behind Next Month
Gamers Can Win Up to $13,900 By Helping Out Popular Open-World RPG
'Players Do Not Realize The Sheer Number of Collabs We've Rejected' Palworld Dev Comments on Terraria Crossover

Mod support has been particularly valuable for sandbox RPGs, where community creators are free to add factions, mechanics, locations, and even entirely new settings long after players exhaust the official content. TaleWorlds' competition gives that process a substantial financial push while encouraging modders to experiment with systems introduced by War Sails , which is something fans don't see every day. With roughly three months to create submissions and €30,000 in total prizes available, the competition could produce content that keeps Mount & Blade 2: Bannerlord feeling fresh well beyond its official updates.

item.title: 'Players Do Not Realize The Sheer Number of Collabs We've Rejected' Palworld Dev Comments on Terraria Crossover
item.description:
A Palworld developer is sharing the company's approach to bringing new collabs to the monster-catching survival game, teasing the significant number of collabs the game has rejected. Palworld has only featured two official in-game collaborations with other games.

The monster-catching survival game from developer Pocketpair has been one of the biggest success stories in gaming since its 2024 early access release. The game quickly caught fire among fans for its combination of a wide array of adorable Pals and its survival gameplay, similar to games like Minecraft . Palworld quickly amassed 8 million sales within the first week of its early access debut, while the game recently launched its long-awaited Version 1.0 update in July 2026, adding many Pals and new areas to explore. Now, one of Palworld 's most outspoken developers is sharing their thoughts on Palworld 's strategy with crossovers.

Palworld Is Officially Expanding to More Platforms

A brand-new, official Palworld spinoff has just been announced, bringing the beloved survival crating game to new platforms later this year.

By Cameron Swan

Palworld Will Only Add Crossovers That "Make Sense"

Pocketpair's Head of Publishing and Communications, Bucky, gave their thoughts on collabs in response to a post about Palworld 's Terraria crossover. Bucky addressed his understanding of some fans' negativity towards the collab, feeling that, while the crossover didn't particularly fit from a lore standpoint, the game takes a "fun-first approach" with its collaborations. Bucky also shared that Pocketpair would not consider a collaboration if it "didn't make sense" for Palworld , hinting at the "sheer number of collabs" that Pocketpair has rejected for not fitting with the game. Bucky did not mention any specific collaborations that Palworld has declined in the past.

Palworld has been relatively light with its in-game collaborations since the game released, only adding two crossovers to the main game. The previously mentioned Terraria crossover was the first official in-game collaboration for the game, adding the Tides of Terraria event with a special crossover dungeon and enemies from Terraria . The game introduced a crossover with Ultrakill in December 2025, adding both the V1 and V2 armor to the game as equipment that players can unlock using Ancient Technology Points. Palworld has not confirmed any future collaborations coming to the game.

Crossovers have become increasingly commonplace in the gaming world in recent years, with many popular games dipping into collaborations. Many games like Fortnite and the Super Smash Bros. series have been built on the strength of their crossovers, bringing popular characters from movies, TV shows, video games, and more together in one game. Even the trading card game industry has continued to see more crossovers, including Magic: The Gathering pushing its Universe Beyond initiative and crossing over with franchises like Lord of the Rings and Marvel.

Palworld is Teasing Its Big Version 1.1 Update
Palworld Releases New Update V1.0.3 for August 2026
Palworld Fan Pays Homage to Destiny 2 With Jaw-Dropping Tower Build

Palworld fans should have plenty to be excited about for the game in the future, whether new crossovers are added or not. Pocketpair recently dropped a teaser about Palworld 's in-development Version 1.1 update, revealing that work has begun on the first update following the game's full release. The developers have also been pushing the game as a full franchise, officially launching a trading card game in late July and revealing a farming sim spinoff in Palworld: Palfarm in late 2025. Palworld is primed to maintain its early success well into the future, with lots on the way for the fledgling franchise.

item.title: Strange World of Warcraft 12.1 Bug Could Be Blizzard Testing a New Feature
item.description:
World of Warcraft players have spotted a new, very strange bug in the 12.1 Curse of Ula'tek update, but it might be Blizzard testing a new feature rather than a glitch. World of Warcraft 's Midnight expansion entered a new season with the release of the Curse of Ula'tek update, adding new content for fans to enjoy, as well as a currently undiscovered Jimothy pet to celebrate the real-life Seattle internet sensation. World of Warcraft patches can sometimes come with bugs, and 12.1 is no exception.

For example, gamers found out that a quest in Undermine is currently bugged, and it takes players on a flying boat that goes out of bounds and disappears from the map. For these reasons and others, such as World of Warcraft 's 12.1 update nerfing the best specs in the game, not all fans are happy with Curse of Ula'tek so far. Others have found joy in the new massive hydra-like pets for the Hunter class, the Amani Troll theme, and the new Coiled Isle, and it seems that reception overall is positive. A new bug is leaving fans puzzled, though, as it allows disconnected players to keep fighting.

World of Warcraft Adding Viral Jimothy The Raccoon as Companion Pet

Blizzard reveals that Jimothy, the short-spined raccoon taking over social media, is coming to World of Warcraft as a companion pet.

By James Ratcliff

New World of Warcraft Bug Makes Disconnected Players Keep Fighting

A new presumed glitch has been found in World of Warcraft 's 12.1 update, Curse of Ula'tek, that makes players who have been disconnected keep fighting enemies. Normally, disconnecting from the game can be problematic during M+ Dungeons and Raids in World of Warcraft , as well as in easier content, because players have to manually reconnect and hope their instance is still there. Instead, there have been reports complete with videos of players being disconnected, only for their characters to keep fighting enemies when in a group. This is likely a bug, especially considering its absence from WoW 's 12.1 patch notes, but some fans are thinking that it might be a way Blizzard is using to test a feature to help players who are disconnected and their teammates.

In fact, WoW 's M+ Dungeons and Raids can be quite difficult at times, and they require a lot of team effort to beat. An example is how a World of Warcraft player got a developer to cheat for them in M+ Dungeons, which sparked a huge debate about resetting leaderboards. If this is a bug, it's a strange one because it's very unlike what normally happens. However, if it is a feature being tested, it could be a major boon for endgame content and retaining instances in the face of disconnections, which can happen to anyone for various reasons. It's also possible that the bug is the presumed feature going live for some users, rather than the fact that it happens at all.

Regardless, Blizzard's MMO remains one of the most loved games ever. Recently, Final Fantasy 14 confirmed it will have a World of Warcraft -inspired update for housing, showing that the game's reach goes well beyond its playerbase.

item.title: Huge Pokemon Leaks Reveal Gen 11 Release Window, Launches Shortly After Winds and Waves
item.description:
Pokemon Winds and Waves haven't even released yet, and already Gen 11 has a launch window it's targeting. While Pokemon Winds and Waves have a release window of late 2027, the following generation of Pokemon games has already begun development, according to newly leaked information. This leak corroborates the internal roadmap for Game Freak's work on the Pokemon series up through 2030.

Although Pokemon Winds and Waves are at the forefront of the franchise as the next official games, having been revealed back in February, Pokemon fans already have a sense of where the future of the series is headed. Leaks indicate that Game Freak has big plans for the Pokemon franchise, and it all seems to be happening in a short timespan. This may be controversial among some fans, given that much of the criticism leveled against the modern Pokemon series is the short turnaround time between new entries, and that doesn't seem to be stopping with Gen 11.

New Pokemon Release Takes You Back to the Hoenn Region

Pokemon fans have a new way to experience the Hoenn Region from Ruby, Sapphire, and Emerald in a brand-new release available right now.

1
By Drew Swanson

Pokemon Gen 11 Started Development in 2024, Targeting 2030 Launch

According to leaked documents shared on Twitter by Centro Leaks, Pokemon Gen 11 began development back in 2024 and is still on track for a 2030 release. Typically, the next generation of Pokemon games begins development once the previous generation is released; Winds and Waves began development in 2022 after Scarlet and Violet launched. However, due to Winds and Waves delays, Gen 11 started early prototyping in 2024, meaning it will likely stay on track for its 2030 release date.

Despite coming from leaks, the information surrounding Pokemon Gen 11 and the future of the franchise comes from official Game Freak documents that were included in the massive TeraLeak last October. As such, it's already established that Game Freak has been planning to release Pokemon Gen 11 in 2030, with other titles releasing in between it and Winds and Waves . While that might seem a bit close to Winds and Waves ' 2027 launch, having a few extra years of development time could result in a better product in the end.

Between Pokemon Winds and Waves and Gen 11, the leaked roadmap from Game Freak includes a variety of other projects at various stages of development:

  • Pokemon Winds and Waves DLC
  • Project Ringo — Said to be the next Pokemon Legends game set in the Galar Region's distant past.
  • Project Seed — Allegedly an ambitious multi-region MMO-like game featuring Kanto, Johto, Hoenn, Sinnoh, and Kitakami all in one interconnected world.
Huge Pokemon Leaks Reveal Gen 11 Release Window, Launches Shortly After Winds and Waves
Brand-New Pokemon Winds and Waves Open-World Details Leak, Including Endgame Features
New Pokemon Winds and Waves Leak Could Mean the End of a 10-Year Era
Pokemon is Officially Leaving Millions of Players Behind in 2027

Given the diversity of projects on Game Freak's plate for the Pokemon series, it's not surprising to learn that Gen 11 has already started development. The scale of these projects sounds like a lot to squeeze into a three-year span, but it becomes much more doable if most or all of these games have been in development for a while longer than fans expect. Pokemon Winds and Waves will have been in development for close to five years by the time the Gen 10 games are released, so it remains to be seen if that development time results in games that are better received by fans.
